text:
# Adult Literacy Lesson Plan
**Theme:** Reading & Completing Everyday Forms and Instructions
**Duration:** 90 minutes | **Group size:** 4–14 adults, mixed ability | **Attendance:** drop-in, irregular

### Design principles behind this plan
- **Self-contained:** nothing depends on what happened last week.
- **Scalable:** activities work whether 4 or 14 people are in the room.
- **Multi-goal:** texts and tasks connect to parenting, driving, employment, and general confidence.
- **Low-exposure:** nobody is forced to read aloud or reveal their level publicly.

---

## Learning Objectives
By the end of the session, learners will be able to:
1. Scan a real-world text to find specific information (date, name, instruction).
2. Complete part of a form using personal or practical details.
3. Identify one new word or skill they can use outside class.

---

## Materials (prepped once, reused weekly with new texts)
- Anchor-task sheets (word search / sentence unscramble) at every seat
- Word Bingo cards + key vocabulary set
- Three tiered real-text packs (laminated):
  - **A – Parent/school:** homework note, consent slip
  - **B – Driving/official:** Highway Code excerpt, mock licence application
  - **C – General/independent:** graded reader, simple newspaper article
- Blank practice forms (medical, consent, job/licence application)
- Individual "Skills Passport" booklets (learner-held; spare blanks for new arrivals)
- Whiteboard, timer, exit slips

---

## Timeline

### 0:00–0:10 | Rolling Start (no fixed beginning)
Anchor task is on the table before anyone arrives — a word search or "copy today's date, write one thing you'd like to read/write better." Learners start as soon as they sit down; no one waits for a "formal" start.
Tutor greets each person individually, briefly checks their Skills Passport (or issues a new one), notes attendance informally.

### 0:10–0:20 | Whole-Group Warm-Up: Key Word Bingo
Call out words relevant to today's texts (*date, signature, name, address, yes/no, licence, school*). Learners mark their cards individually or in pairs (pair up automatically if numbers are higher).
Purpose: oral/visual recognition, confidence-building, no writing exposure yet.

### 0:20–0:35 | Explicit Mini-Lesson (whole group)
Tutor models reading one short real text aloud using **think-aloud scanning**: *"I look for the date first… I look for a word I recognise…"*
Teach **one transferable skill**: scanning for key information rather than decoding every word.
Differentiate through questioning, not grouping: easier questions ("What letter does this start with?") alongside harder ones ("What does this sentence tell you to do?") addressed to different individuals.

### 0:35–1:05 | Flexible Stations (core block — works at any group size)
Set up 3–4 self-contained stations, each with instruction cards and an answer key so learners can self- or peer-check:

| Station | Focus | Task range (tiered within same text) |
|---|---|---|
| A – Parent/school texts | Reading a note, replying | "Find 3 words you know" → "Write a one-sentence reply" |
| B – Driving/official forms | Highway Code + application form | "Circle the date" → "Fill in the form correctly" |
| C – Independent reading corner | Graded reader/newspaper, audio-assist option | Self-paced, quiet |
| D – Tutor table | 1:1 or small-group support | Phonics, writing practice, tailored to individual |

- **4 learners:** free movement between 2 stations, tutor floats throughout.
- **14 learners:** split into small groups, rotate every ~10 minutes, or allow free-choice movement to cut down management load. Use a confident regular as an informal "lead" at one station if needed.
- **Peer buddy system:** pair newcomers or less confident learners with a regular attender — supports irregular attendance invisibly.

### 1:05–1:20 | Goal-Linked Application Task
Choice board on the wall: *"Fill in a practice licence form," "Write a note to your child's teacher," "Complete a job application line."* Learners pick the task matching their own reason for attending.
Tutor circulates for brief 1:1 check-ins, noting progress in each Skills Passport.

### 1:20–1:30 | Plenary & Forward Look
Whole group reconvenes.
- Quick pair-share: "Tell your neighbour one thing you can read or fill in now that you couldn't an hour ago."
- Tutor adds one line to each learner's Skills Passport.
- One-sentence preview of next week's theme, with explicit reassurance: *"You don't need to have been here last week — just come along."*
- Anonymous exit slip: two tick-boxes ("Useful today," "Want more practice on…") — minimal writing required.

---

## Contingency & Adaptation Notes
- **Small group (4):** skip timed rotations; let people move at their own pace; more 1:1 tutor time naturally available.
- **Large group (14):** use a timer and peer leads; rely more on the choice board to spread tutor attention; keep instructions on cards so stations run without constant tutor input.
- **Latecomers:** anchor task always available; stations can be joined mid-stream since each is self-contained.
- **Returning after an absence:** no need to "catch up" — the Skills Passport tracks individual progress independently of group continuity.
- **Mixed ability:** every text exists in 2–3 difficulty tiers on the same topic, so no one is excluded or under-challenged.
- **Confidence protection:** no compulsory reading aloud; think-pair-share, pointing, and written responses are always valid alternatives.
